title: Plate with a circular hole under tension: Kirsch stress concentration (analytic)
description:
Quarter model of a large plate with a traction-free hole of radius a at the origin corner, pulled along x by a remote stress S (boundary_load t_x = S on x_hi); rollers on x_lo and y_lo are the two symmetry lines, y_hi is free. Plane strain, static.
Analytic (Kirsch, infinite plate, independent of E and nu): with q = a^2 / r^2, c2 = cos 2theta, c4 = cos 4theta: sigma_xx = S (1 - q (3/2 c2 + c4) + 3/2 q^2 c4), sigma_yy = -S (q (c2/2 - c4) + 3/2 q^2 c4). On the y axis sigma_xx = S (1 + a^2 / 2y^2 + 3a^4 / 2y^4) (3 S at the hole), on the x axis sigma_yy = S/2 (a^2/x^2 - 3a^4/x^4) (-S at the hole) and sigma_xx = S (1 - 5a^2 / 2x^2 + 3a^4 / 2x^4).
Line profile tab: sxx_y_axis (solid.stress_xx up the y axis), syy_x_axis and sxx_x_axis (along the x axis); the lines run half a cell off the axes through the cell centres and start a quarter cell outside the hole (a start on the hole edge can sample the void cell, stress 0); the curves use the full Kirsch field at the sampled cell centres. Errors relative to each curve's range: ~1-2 % rms and up to ~13 % (sxx_y_axis; ~5 % syy_x_axis, ~3 % sxx_x_axis) in the cell next to the hole: the hole is a staircase of 32 cells per radius (the first cell or two at the hole scatter more) and the plate is finite (width 24 a: the peak rises ~0.7 %, the far field carries the load the hole removes).
Derived values tab: F_left = x_lo roller reaction vs -S L (exact equilibrium, ~1e-8); sxx_peak (probe in the cell next to the hole on the y axis, ~2.9 S) and sxx_near (4 cells further out) vs Kirsch at the probe points (~9 % low next to the staircase, ~3 % high further out: the ligament still carries the whole load).
Field tab: von Mises and stress maps.
